scope: Finite adaptive rear recovery and oncoming crossing boundary

source.intent: HBQ chooses a longer smooth back-off with room, otherwise a shorter one; rear-first requests and temporary yielding preserve space. Separate lateral shifts and route replanning help opposing traffic pass.
source.redesign: No source EachFrame push, physics movement or route reconstruction copied. Use existing native finite recovery, body/support observation and exact current-owner journal.

implementation: One8m rear clearance preference; only named spatial obstruction/support reasons allow one3.5m fallback. Actual supported destination comes from the selected observer. Public rearEnvelope stores8/6 or3.5/2 clearance/native BACK travel limit; legacy receipts default8/6, other envelopes fail active proof. Active observation uses remaining travel plus original positive end buffer; original heading/damage/lateral/overshoot bounds still apply. This avoids repeatedly demanding the full initial clearance behind an already backing vehicle. Original deadlines and retry count remain unchanged.
cost: At most one additional bounded RearClear call per eligible rear admission attempt, not every ordinary callback. Worst-case two observer calls, each retaining its own64actor/250m/70ray bound. Active-leg observer count unchanged. No new worker/global scan; actual runtime cost unmeasured.
headOnGap: Existing DrivingPassPlan refuses >25degree heading difference, so it cannot provide an oncoming crossing plan unchanged. HBQ lateral push cannot be replaced by rear travel alone. Native side-clear geometry, stable yield choice, complete crossing and held parent/leaf handback remain required before queue activation.
